response.consequence: Creating a Google Meet booking for a host with no destination calendar throws a TypeError in `EventManager.create`. The booking creation or confirmation fails. Before this change, the code fell back to Cal Video.
response.explanation: The change makes `destinationCalendar` an array. The callers in confirm.handler, editLocation.handler and bookingReminder now pass `[]` when neither the booking nor the user has a destination calendar. `EventManager.create` runs `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];`, which is `undefined` for an empty array or a missing value. The next line then reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` with no optional chaining. The old code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`, which was safe. For any event whose location is Google Meet and which has no destination calendar, this throws a TypeError.
response.title: Meet fallback dereferences undefined when destinationCalendar is an empty array

response.consequence: On instances with team billing disabled, newly created organizations have no slug and no requestedSlug. The org subdomain and its routing are then broken, and the slug cannot be recovered from metadata.
response.explanation: The old code was `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })`, which set the slug when billing was disabled. The change rewrote it as `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}` and dropped the negation. The slug is now set only when billing is enabled, which is the opposite of before. That is also the only case where `requestedSlug` is stored. When billing is enabled, the org gets its slug immediately, and the pending-slug flow in `requestedSlug` is no longer a separate step. When billing is disabled (the self-hosted default), the org is created with neither `slug` nor `requestedSlug`.
response.title: Organization slug condition inverted: slug only set when team billing is enabled

response.consequence: The event is not created on those team members' destination calendars. Booking-level destinationCalendar is also left unset.
response.explanation: evt.destinationCalendar is set to null when neither eventType.destinationCalendar nor organizerUser.destinationCalendar exists. The following `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is then a silent no-op, so the destination calendars collected from the other COLLECTIVE hosts are discarded. Failing case: a collective event where the organizer has no destination calendar but another host does. The array is null and that host's calendar is never used.
response.title: Collective team members' destination calendars dropped when organizer/event type has none

response.explanation: The class field type destinationCalendar is now DestinationCalendar[] | null, which matches the CalendarEvent interface in packages/types/Calendar.d.ts:171. The new optional externalId on EventResult is additive.

response.consequence: When the caller passes no externalCalendarId, deleting a Google event targets the user's primary calendar instead of the booking's destination calendar, so the event is not found or not removed. Updating an event with no calendarId fails the API call.
response.explanation: The fallback branch only runs when externalCalendarId is falsy, but it searches destinationCalendar for an entry whose externalId === externalCalendarId. That compares against a falsy value, so it never matches a real calendar and the result is undefined. The old code fell back to destinationCalendar.externalId. In deleteEvent (line 317) the calendarId then becomes "primary". In updateEvent (line 256) selectedCalendar is undefined, so events.update gets no calendarId.

other_findings.consequence: Google events.update is called without a calendarId when the caller omits externalCalendarId.
other_findings.explanation: This is the same defect in updateEvent. When externalCalendarId is falsy, the lookup compares each cal.externalId to that falsy value and returns undefined, so selectedCalendar is undefined. The old code used destinationCalendar.externalId.
